title.zh: 第一 律曆上 律準 候氣
title.en: Volume 91: Rhythm and the Calendar Part One
title.raw: 第一 律曆上 律準 候氣 Volume 91: Rhythm and the Calendar Part One

sentences.zh: 後漢書志第一 律曆上 律準候氣

translations.literal: Later Han Treatises part one: Pitch standards and calendar part one—pitch regulators and qi observation.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise I of the Later Han: musical pitch (upper scroll)—regulators for tuning pipes and the qi-detection method.

sentences.zh: 古之人論數也，曰：「物生而後有象，像而後有滋，滋而後有數」。

translations.literal: The ancients, discussing number, said: “Things arise and then there are images; from images there is growth; from growth there are numbers.”
translations.idiomatic: Ancient thinkers defined reckoning in stages: "beings yield forms, forms yield proliferation, and only then do numbers apply."

sentences.zh: 然則天地初形，人物既著，則筭數之事生矣。

translations.literal: Thus once heaven and earth first took shape and human beings stood forth, the arts of counting began.
translations.idiomatic: Once heaven, earth, and humanity existed, mathematics followed inevitably.

sentences.zh: 記稱大橈作甲子[1]，隸首作數[2]。

translations.literal: Records name Da Nao as creator of the sexagenary cycle note one and Li Shou as creator of numeration note two.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition credits Da Nao with the stem-branch cycle note one and Li Shou with systematic numbering note two.

sentences.zh: 二者既立，以比日表[3]，以管萬事。

translations.literal: With both established they matched solar shadows note three and governed the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Those tools calibrated gnomon shadows note three and ordered every administrative reckoning.

sentences.zh: 夫一、十、百、千、萬，所同用也；

translations.literal: One, ten, hundred, thousand, and myriad are what all reckonings share;
translations.idiomatic: Digits from one through myriad underpin every tally;

sentences.zh: 律、度、量、衡、歷，其別用也。

translations.literal: pitch pipes, length, capacity, weight, and calendar are where applications diverge.
translations.idiomatic: but pitch, linear measure, volume, balance, and celestial reckoning each branch separately.

sentences.zh: 故體有長短，檢以度[4]；

translations.literal: Hence bodies have length—checked by graduated rules note four;
translations.idiomatic: Bodies are gauged with rulers note four;

sentences.zh: 物有多少，受以量[5]；

translations.literal: things come in quantity—received into vessels note five;
translations.idiomatic: bulk is poured into standard measures note five;

sentences.zh: 量有輕重，平以權衡[6]；

translations.literal: loads differ in weight—balanced by steelyards note six;
translations.idiomatic: weight rests on beam balances note six;

sentences.zh: 聲有清濁，協以律呂；

translations.literal: tones differ in clarity or dullness—harmonized through the twelve pitch-classes;
translations.idiomatic: sound divides into clear and muddy tones harmonized by the pitch-cycle;

sentences.zh: 三光運行，紀以歷數：然後幽隱之情，精微之變，可得而綜也[7]。

translations.literal: the three luminaries wheel overhead—registered by calendrical numbers: after this hidden tendencies and subtle transformations may be grasped in synthesis note seven.
translations.idiomatic: sun, moon, and stars ride calendrical mathematics note seven until even arcane shifts yield to systematic grasp.

sentences.zh: 漢興，北平侯張蒼首治律歷。

translations.literal: When Han arose Marquis Zhang Cang of Beiping first regulated pitch pipes and the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynastic founding Zhang Cang of Beiping Marquis reorganized harmonics and astronomy.

sentences.zh: 孝武正樂，置協律之官。

translations.literal: Filial Emperor Wu corrected ritual music and founded offices for harmonizing pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu standardized court music and appointed specialists to tune the bells.

sentences.zh: 至元始中，博徵通知鐘律者，考其意義，羲和劉歆典領條奏，前史班固取以為志。

translations.literal: By the Yuanshi era court broadly summoned masters versed in bells and pitch, examined their doctrines, and Astronomy Director Liu Xin drafted systematic memorials that Former Han historian Ban Gu excerpted into his treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi-era commissions collected tuning theory; Liu Xin’s Directorate of Astronomy codified it for the throne, and Ban Gu folded that dossier into his monographs.

sentences.zh: 而元帝時，郎中京房，房字君明，知五聲之音，六律之數。

translations.literal: Meanwhile under Yuan Emperor, palace attendant Jing Fang—styled Junming—mastered the five degrees of tone and the mathematics of the six pitch-classes.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Jing Fang (Junming), contemporary with Yuan Emperor, knew the five tones and six-pitch arithmetic inside out.

sentences.zh: 上使太子太傅韋玄成、字少翁諫議大夫章，雜試問房於樂府。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered heir-apparent tutor Wei Xuancheng—styled Shao Weng—and advisory counselor Zhang to examine Fang jointly inside the Bureau of Music.
translations.idiomatic: The throne tasked Wei Xuancheng and Counselor Zhang with cross-examining him at the imperial conservatory.

sentences.zh: 房對：「受學故小黃令焦延壽。

translations.literal: Fang replied: “My teacher was former district magistrate of Xiaohuang Jiao Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang answered: “I studied under former Xiaohuang magistrate Jiao Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 六十律相生之法：以上生下，皆三生二，以下生上，皆三生四，陽下生陰，陰上生陽，終於中呂，而十二律畢矣。

translations.literal: The mutual-production rule among sixty pitch-classes: generating downward from high always applies thrice-two reduction; generating upward from low always applies thrice-four augmentation; yang generates yin below and yin generates yang above, finishing at Zhonglü so the twelve pipes complete.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-pitch derivation uses three-halves downward steps and four-thirds upward steps until Zhonglü closes the duodecimal set.

sentences.zh: 中呂上生執始，執始下生去滅，上下相生，終於南事，六十律畢矣。

translations.literal: Zhonglü generates Zhishi above; Zhishi generates Qumie below; alternating above and below production ends at Nanshi, completing sixty tones.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglü ascends to Zhishi, Zhishi descends to Qumie, and the ladder finishes at Nanshi—sixty names in all.

sentences.zh: 夫十二律之變至於六十，猶八卦之變至於六十四也。

translations.literal: Twelve pitch-classes ramifying to sixty parallels how eight trigrams ramify to sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pipes blooming into sixty notes mirrors eight trigrams blooming into sixty-four hexagrams.

sentences.zh: 宓羲作易，紀陽氣之初，以為律法。

translations.literal: Fuxi composed the Changes, marking the first emergence of yang qi to serve as law for pitch computation.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi’s Zhou yi anchors yang qi’s primal emergence—the same logic pitch computation follows.

sentences.zh: 建日冬至之聲，以黃鐘為宮，太蔟為商，姑洗為角，林鐘為徵，南呂為羽，應鐘為變宮，蕤賓為變徵[8]。

translations.literal: Naming the sound that belongs to the winter solstice jian day: Huangzhong serves as gong, Taicu as shang, Guxian as jue, Linzhong as zhi, Nanlü as yu, Yingzhong as altered gong, Ruibin as altered zhi note eight.
translations.idiomatic: On the jian day of midwinter you tune Huangzhong to keynote gong, slot Taicu as shang, Guxian as jue, Linzhong as zhi, Nanlü as yu, Yingzhong as biangong, Ruibin as bianzhi note eight.

sentences.zh: 此聲氣之元，五音之正也。

translations.literal: These are the root of tone-breath and the orthodox alignment of the pentatonic scale.
translations.idiomatic: That cluster forms the acoustic foundation and canonical pentatonic template.

sentences.zh: 故各終一日。

translations.literal: Thus each rules one full day.
translations.idiomatic: Each configuration therefore governs an entire day.

sentences.zh: 其餘以次運行，當日者各自為宮，而商徵以類從焉[9]。

translations.literal: The remainder rotate in sequence; whichever tone sits on the given day becomes gong for that day while shang and zhi follow by category note nine.
translations.idiomatic: Other days rotate the pattern; the daily tonic becomes gong while shang and zhi shift by analogy note nine.

sentences.zh: 禮運篇曰『五聲、六律、十二管還相為宮』，此之謂也[10]。

translations.literal: The “Evolution of Rites” chapter says “five tones, six pitch-classes, and twelve pipes succeed one another as gong”—this is what it means note ten.
translations.idiomatic: The Liyun line about twelve tubes cyclically serving as keynote captures exactly this note ten.

sentences.zh: 以六十律分朞之日，黃鐘自冬至始，及冬至而復，陰陽寒燠風雨之占生焉。

translations.literal: Apportioning the sixty pitch-classes across the days of the cycle: Huangzhong opens at winter solstice and returns there; omens of yin-yang, cold, heat, wind, and rain arise from it.
translations.idiomatic: Splitting sixty tones across the calendar begins and ends at Huangzhong on midwinter day, feeding weather divination.

sentences.zh: 於以檢攝羣音，考其高下，苟非草木之聲，則無不有所合。

translations.literal: With it one reins in every sounding note, compares relative height, and except for sounds from plants or trees nothing fails to register agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Against that grid every musical tone lines up unless it is mere rustling vegetation.

sentences.zh: 虞書曰『律和聲』，此之謂也。」

translations.literal: The Shang shu says “pitch harmonizes sound”—this is the sense intended.”
translations.idiomatic: “Thus,” he concluded, “the Documents command pitch to harmonize voice.”

sentences.zh: 房又曰：「竹聲不可以度調，故作準以定數。

translations.literal: Fang added: “Bamboo pipes cannot be regulated by abstract measure, so I fashioned a pitch regulator to fix the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Fang continued: “Because bamboo defies abstract calibration, I built a tuning regulator to nail the ratios.

sentences.zh: 準之狀如瑟，長丈而十三弦，隱閒九尺，以應黃鐘之律九寸；

translations.literal: Shaped like a se zither, one zhang long with thirteen strings, its concealed span nine chi matching Huangzhong’s nine cun pipe;
translations.idiomatic: It resembles a se: thirteen strings over one zhang, nine chi of vibrating length answering Huangzhong’s nine-cun tube;

sentences.zh: 中央一弦，下有畫分寸，以為六十律清濁之節。」

translations.literal: the central string bears ruled inch-marks below as gradations for the sixty pitch-classes’ bright or dull nodes.”
translations.idiomatic: its middle string carries engraved fen and cun used to mark every bright or dull step among sixty tones."

sentences.zh: 房言律詳於歆所奏，其術施行於史官，候部用之。

translations.literal: Fang’s exposition exceeded Xin’s memorial in detail; his method operated in the archives and the qi-watch offices adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: His theory ran deeper than Liu Xin’s submission and became standard for historians and seasonal qi observers.

sentences.zh: 文多不悉載。

translations.literal: The text is too lengthy to copy entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Most detail is omitted here for length.

sentences.zh: 故總其本要，以續前志。

translations.literal: Therefore I summarize the essentials to extend the prior treatise.
translations.idiomatic: This section condenses the core to continue the earlier monograph.

sentences.zh: 律術曰：陽以圓為形，其性動。

translations.literal: Pitch doctrine says: yang takes the circle as its figure and its nature is active.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonic theory: yang manifests as round motion and tends toward movement.

sentences.zh: 陰以方為節，其性靜。

translations.literal: Yin takes the square as its norm and its nature is still.
translations.idiomatic: Yin squares itself into boundaries and stays quiescent.

sentences.zh: 動者數三，靜者數二。

translations.literal: What moves counts by three; what rests counts by two.
translations.idiomatic: Active numbers ride three; static numbers ride two.

sentences.zh: 以陽生陰，倍之；

translations.literal: When yang begets yin, double it;
translations.idiomatic: Yang generating yin doubles the prior value;

sentences.zh: 以陰生陽，四之：皆三而一。

translations.literal: when yin begets yang, quadruple it—both cases divide by three once.
translations.idiomatic: yin generating yang multiplies by four before the universal division by three.

sentences.zh: 陽生陰曰下生，陰生陽曰上生。

translations.literal: Yang producing yin is called lower generation; yin producing yang is called upper generation.
translations.idiomatic: Down-generation lowers the pipe; up-generation raises it.

sentences.zh: 上生不得過黃鐘之清濁，下生不得及黃鐘之數實。

translations.literal: Upper generation must not exceed Huangzhong’s bright or dull limit; lower generation must not fall short of Huangzhong’s numerical solidity.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending steps cannot surpass Huangzhong’s upper bound; descending steps cannot undershoot its canonical mass-number.

sentences.zh: 皆參天兩地，圓蓋方覆，六耦承奇之道也。

translations.literal: All this mirrors “three parts heaven, two parts earth,” round heaven covering square earth—paired even forces bearing odd potency.
translations.idiomatic: The arithmetic embodies heaven-three earth-two, dome over square plane, even couples lifting odd centers.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘，律呂之首，而生十二律者也[11]。

translations.literal: Huangzhong heads the pitch-cycle and begets the twelve classes note eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong seeds every subsequent pipe note eleven.

sentences.zh: 其相生也，皆三分而損益之。

translations.literal: Their mutual production always applies thirding with subtraction or addition.
translations.idiomatic: Each link applies the classical subtract-one-third or add-one-third rule.

sentences.zh: 是故十二律之，得十七萬七千一百四十七，是為黃鐘之實[12]。

translations.literal: Hence working through the twelve pitch-values yields 177,147, which is Huangzhong’s solidity note twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve iterations therefore pile to 177,147—the canonical Huangzhong “solid” note twelve.

sentences.zh: 又以二乘而三約之，是為下生林鐘之實。

translations.literal: Multiply by two and divide by three to obtain the solidity for Linzhong generated below.
translations.idiomatic: Two-thirds of that mass defines down-generated Linzhong.

sentences.zh: 又以四乘而三約之，是為上生太蔟之實。

translations.literal: Multiply by four and divide by three to obtain the solidity for Taicu generated above.
translations.idiomatic: Four-thirds steps back upward to Taicu’s mass.

sentences.zh: 推此上下，以定六十律之實。

translations.literal: Extend this alternation to settle the solidity figures for all sixty pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the ladder to enumerate sixty tonal solids.

sentences.zh: 以九三之，數萬九千六百八十三為法。

translations.literal: Divide repeatedly by nine-cubed (729); 19,683 becomes the divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Use 19,683—nine cubed times three—as the modular divisor.

sentences.zh: 律為寸，於準為尺。

translations.literal: Where pitch reads in cun the regulator reads in chi.
translations.idiomatic: Pipe lengths translate to chi on the regulator at ten-to-one scale.

sentences.zh: 不盈者十之，所得為分。

translations.literal: Remainders scale by tens to yield fen.
translations.idiomatic: Fractional remainders become fen by decimal promotion.

sentences.zh: 又不盈十之，所得為小分。

translations.literal: Still indivisible remainders scale again by ten for small fen.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller scraps refine again into micro-fen.

sentences.zh: 以其餘正其強弱。

translations.literal: Use the leftover bits to calibrate relative strength or weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Residual micro-units mark acoustic strong or weak bias.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘，十七萬七千一百四十七。

translations.literal: Huangzhong: 177,147.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong solid: 177,147.

sentences.zh: 下生林鐘。

translations.literal: Generates Linzhong below.
translations.idiomatic: Down-generates Linzhong.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘為宮，太蔟商，林鐘徵。

translations.literal: Huangzhong as gong, Taicu as shang, Linzhong as zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mode: Huangzhong tonic, Taicu shang, Linzhong zhi.

sentences.zh: 一日律九寸，準九尺。

translations.literal: Pipe length nine cun; regulator length nine chi.
translations.idiomatic: Nine cun on the pipe, nine chi on the regulator.

sentences.zh: 色育，十七萬六千七百七十六。

translations.idiomatic: Seyu solid: 176,776.

sentences.zh: 下生謙待。

translations.literal: Generates Qiandai below.
translations.idiomatic: Down-generates Qiandai.

sentences.zh: 色育為宮，未知商，謙待徵。

translations.literal: Seyu as gong, shang unknown, Qiandai as zhi.
translations.idiomatic: With Seyu as tonic the matching shang pipe goes unrecorded; Qiandai supplies zhi.

sentences.zh: 六日。

translations.literal: Six days.
translations.idiomatic: Occupies six days in the cycle.

sentences.zh: 律，八寸九分小分八微強。

translations.literal: Pipe: eight cun nine fen plus eight micro-fen, slightly strong.
translations.idiomatic: Pipe measure 8.98+ strong micro-fen.

sentences.zh: 準，八尺九寸萬五千九百七十三。

translations.literal: Regulator: eight chi nine cun plus 15,973 micro-units.
translations.idiomatic: Regulator line 8 chi 9 cun and 15,973 residual ticks.

sentences.zh: 執始，十七萬四千七百六十二。

translations.literal: Zhishi: 174,762.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishi solid: 174,762.

sentences.zh: 下生去滅。

translations.literal: Generates Qumie below.
translations.idiomatic: Down-generates Qumie.

sentences.zh: 執始為宮，時息商，去滅徵。

translations.literal: Zhishi as gong, Shixi as shang, Qumie as zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mode: Zhishi gong, Shixi shang, Qumie zhi.

sentences.zh: 六日。

translations.literal: Six days.
translations.idiomatic: Six-day span.

sentences.zh: 律，八寸八分小分七大強。

translations.literal: Pipe: eight cun eight fen plus seven micro-fen, greatly strong.
translations.idiomatic: Pipe 8.87+ marked strong.

sentences.zh: 準，八尺八寸萬五千五百一十六。

translations.literal: Regulator: eight chi eight cun plus 15,516 micro-units.
translations.idiomatic: Regulator 8 chi 8 cun, remainder 15,516.

sentences.zh: 丙盛，十七萬二千四百一十。

translations.literal: Bingsheng: 172,410.
translations.idiomatic: Bingsheng solid: 172,410.

sentences.zh: 下生安度。

translations.literal: Generates Andu below.
translations.idiomatic: Down-generates Andu.

sentences.zh: 丙盛為宮，屈齊商，安度徵。

translations.literal: Bingsheng as gong, Juqi as shang, Andu as zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mode: Bingsheng gong, Juqi shang, Andu zhi.

sentences.zh: 六日。

translations.literal: Six days.
translations.idiomatic: Six days.

sentences.zh: 律，八寸七分小分六微弱。

translations.literal: Pipe: eight cun seven fen plus six micro-fen, slightly weak.
translations.idiomatic: Pipe 8.76 slightly weak.

sentences.zh: 準，八尺七寸萬一千六百七十九。

translations.literal: Regulator: eight chi seven cun plus 11,679 micro-units.
translations.idiomatic: Regulator 8 chi 7 cun, remainder 11,679.

sentences.zh: 分動，十七萬八十九。

translations.literal: Fendong: 170,089.
translations.idiomatic: Fendong solid: 170,089.

sentences.zh: 下生歸嘉。

translations.literal: Generates Guijia below.
translations.idiomatic: Down-generates Guijia.

sentences.zh: 分動為宮，隨期商，歸嘉徵。

translations.literal: Fendong as gong, Suiqi as shang, Guijia as zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mode: Fendong gong, Suiqi shang, Guijia zhi.

sentences.zh: 六日。

translations.literal: Six days.
translations.idiomatic: Six-day allocation.

sentences.zh: 律，八寸六分小分四強。

translations.literal: Pipe: eight cun six fen plus four micro-fen, strong.
translations.idiomatic: Pipe 8.64 strong.

sentences.zh: 準，八尺六寸八千一百五十二。

translations.literal: Regulator: eight chi six cun plus 8,152 micro-units.
translations.idiomatic: Regulator 8 chi 6 cun, remainder 8,152.

sentences.zh: 質末，十六萬七千八百。

translations.idiomatic: Zimo solid: 167,800.

sentences.zh: 下生否與。

translations.literal: Generates Fouyu below.
translations.idiomatic: Down-generates Fouyu.

sentences.zh: 質末為宮，形晉商，否與徵。

translations.literal: Zimo as gong, Xingjin as shang, Fouyu as zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mode: Zimo gong, Xingjin shang, Fouyu zhi.

sentences.zh: 六日。

translations.literal: Six days.
translations.idiomatic: Six days.

sentences.zh: 律，八寸五分小分二強。

translations.literal: Pipe: eight cun five fen plus two micro-fen, strong.
translations.idiomatic: Pipe 8.52 strong.

sentences.zh: 準，八尺五寸四千九百四十五。

translations.literal: Regulator: eight chi five cun plus 4,945 micro-units.
translations.idiomatic: Regulator 8 chi 5 cun, remainder 4,945.

sentences.zh: 大呂，十六萬五千八百八十八。

translations.idiomatic: Dalü solid: 165,888.

sentences.zh: 下生夷則。

translations.literal: Generates Yize below.
translations.idiomatic: Down-generates Yize.

sentences.zh: 大呂為宮，夾鐘商，夷則徵。

translations.literal: Dalü as gong, Jiazhong as shang, Yize as zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mode: Dalü gong, Jiazhong shang, Yize zhi.

sentences.zh: 八日。

translations.literal: Eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Eight-day span.

sentences.zh: 律，八寸四分小分三弱。

translations.literal: Pipe: eight cun four fen plus three micro-fen, weak.
translations.idiomatic: Pipe 8.43 weak.

sentences.zh: 準，八尺四寸五千五百八。

translations.literal: Regulator: eight chi four cun plus 5,508 micro-units.
translations.idiomatic: Regulator 8 chi 4 cun, remainder 5,508.

sentences.zh: 分否，十六萬三千六百五十四。

translations.literal: Fenfou: 163,654.
translations.idiomatic: Fenfou solid: 163,654.

sentences.zh: 下生解形。

translations.literal: Generates Jiexing below.
translations.idiomatic: Down-generates Jiexing.

sentences.zh: 分否為宮，開時商，解形徵。

translations.literal: Fenfou as gong, Kaishi as shang, Jiexing as zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mode: Fenfou gong, Kaishi shang, Jiexing zhi.

sentences.zh: 八日。

translations.literal: Eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Eight days.

sentences.zh: 律，八寸三分小分一強。

translations.literal: Pipe: eight cun three fen plus one micro-fen, strong.
translations.idiomatic: Pipe 8.31 strong.

sentences.zh: 準，八尺三寸二千八百五十一。

translations.literal: Regulator: 8 chi 3 cun plus 2,851 micro-units.
translations.idiomatic: Regulator: 8 chi 3 cun plus 2,851 micro-units.

sentences.zh: 凌陰，十六萬一千四百五十二。

translations.literal: Lingyin: 161,452.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyin solidity: 161,452.

sentences.zh: 下生去南。

translations.literal: Generates Qunan below.
translations.idiomatic: Down-generates Qunan.

sentences.zh: 凌陰為宮，族嘉商，去南徵。

translations.literal: Lingyin as gong, Zujia as shang, Qunan as zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mode: Lingyin tonic, Zujia shang, Qunan zhi.

sentences.zh: 八日。

translations.literal: 8 days.

sentences.zh: 截管為律，吹以考聲，列以物氣，道之本也[13]。

translations.literal: Cutting pipes to make pitch-pipes, blowing them to test the sounds, and arranging them according to the qi of things is the root of the method [13].
translations.idiomatic: Cutting pipes to make pitch-pipes, blowing them to test the sounds, and arranging them according to the qi of things is the root of the method [13].

sentences.zh: 術家以其聲微而體難知，其分數不明，故作準以代之。

translations.literal: Because specialists found their sounds subtle and their substance hard to know, and because the fractional measurements were unclear, they made the zhun to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Because specialists found their sounds subtle and their substance hard to know, and because the fractional measurements were unclear, they made the zhun to replace them.

sentences.zh: 準之聲，明暢易達，分寸又粗。

translations.literal: The sound of the zhun is clear, resonant, and easy to grasp, and its measurements in fen and cun are also coarser.
translations.idiomatic: The sound of the zhun is clear, resonant, and easy to grasp, and its measurements in fen and cun are also coarser.

sentences.zh: 然弦以緩急清濁，非管無以正也。

translations.literal: Yet strings depend on slackness and tightness for clear and turbid tones; without pipes there is no way to correct them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet strings depend on slackness and tightness for clear and turbid tones; without pipes there is no way to correct them.

sentences.zh: 均其中弦，令與黃鐘相得，案畫以求諸律，無不如數而應者矣。

translations.literal: When its central string is tuned to correspond with Huangzhong, the marked divisions can be used to seek the several pitch-pipes, and none fails to respond according to the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: When its central string is tuned to correspond with Huangzhong, the marked divisions can be used to seek the several pitch-pipes, and none fails to respond according to the numbers.

sentences.zh: 音聲精微，綜之者解。

translations.literal: Sounds are subtle and minute; those who gather them together understand them.
translations.idiomatic: Sounds are subtle and minute; those who gather them together understand them.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，待詔候鐘律殷肜上言：「官無曉六十律以準調音者。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe, Yin Rong, Expectant Appointee for Observing the Bells and Pitch-Pipes, submitted: "Among the officials, no one understands the sixty pitch-pipes well enough to tune sounds with the zhun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe, Yin Rong, Expectant Appointee for Observing the Bells and Pitch-Pipes, submitted: "Among the officials, no one understands the sixty pitch-pipes well enough to tune sounds with the zhun.

sentences.zh: 故待詔嚴崇具以準法教子男宣，宣通習。

translations.literal: The former Expectant Appointee Yan Chong fully taught the method of the zhun to his son Xuan, and Xuan mastered it.
translations.idiomatic: The former Expectant Appointee Yan Chong fully taught the method of the zhun to his son Xuan, and Xuan mastered it.

sentences.zh: 願召宣補學官，主調樂器。」

translations.literal: I request that Xuan be summoned and appointed to an academic office, to take charge of tuning musical instruments."
translations.idiomatic: I request that Xuan be summoned and appointed to an academic office, to take charge of tuning musical instruments."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「崇子學審曉律，別其族，協其聲者，審試。

translations.literal: The edict said: "If Chong's son has studied and truly understands the pitch-pipes, distinguishes their families, and harmonizes their sounds, he should be carefully tested.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "If Chong's son has studied and truly understands the pitch-pipes, distinguishes their families, and harmonizes their sounds, he should be carefully tested.

sentences.zh: 不得依托父學，以聾為聰。

translations.literal: He must not rely on his father's learning and treat deafness as hearing.
translations.idiomatic: He must not rely on his father's learning and treat deafness as hearing.

sentences.zh: 聲微妙，獨非莫知，獨是莫曉。

translations.literal: Sound is subtle and wondrous: if one alone says it is wrong, no one knows; if one alone says it is right, no one understands.
translations.idiomatic: Sound is subtle and wondrous: if one alone says it is wrong, no one knows; if one alone says it is right, no one understands.

sentences.zh: 以律錯吹，能知命十二律不失一，方為能傳崇學耳。」

translations.literal: Only if the pitch-pipes are blown in mixed order and he can identify the twelve pitch-pipes without missing one may he be considered able to transmit Chong's learning."
translations.idiomatic: Only if the pitch-pipes are blown in mixed order and he can identify the twelve pitch-pipes without missing one may he be considered able to transmit Chong's learning."

sentences.zh: 太史丞弘試十二律，其二中，其四不中，其六不知何律，宣遂罷。

translations.literal: Assistant Grand Scribe Hong tested the twelve pitch-pipes: two were correct, four were incorrect, and for six he did not know which pitch-pipes they were, so Xuan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Grand Scribe Hong tested the twelve pitch-pipes: two were correct, four were incorrect, and for six he did not know which pitch-pipes they were, so Xuan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 自此律家莫能為準施弦，候部莫知復見[14]。

translations.literal: From then on, no pitch specialist could string the zhun, and the Office of Observations no longer knew how to see it restored [14].
translations.idiomatic: From then on, no pitch specialist could string the zhun, and the Office of Observations no longer knew how to see it restored [14].

sentences.zh: 熹平六年，東觀召典律者太子舍人張光等問準意。

translations.literal: In Xiping 6, the Eastern Lodge summoned Zhang Guang, a Crown Prince's retainer who handled the pitch-pipes, and others to ask about the meaning of the zhun.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiping 6, the Eastern Lodge summoned Zhang Guang, a Crown Prince's retainer who handled the pitch-pipes, and others to ask about the meaning of the zhun.

sentences.zh: 光等不知，歸閱舊藏，乃得其器，形制如房書，猶不能定其弦緩急，音不可書以時人，知之者欲教而無從，心達者體知而無師，故史官能辨清濁者遂絕。

translations.literal: Guang and the others did not know. They returned and examined the old storehouses, where they found the instrument. Its form matched Fang's writings, but they still could not determine the slackness or tightness of its strings. The sounds could not be written down for people of the time; those who knew them wished to teach but had no starting point, and those whose minds grasped them understood physically but had no teacher. Thus the scribal officials able to distinguish clear and turbid tones disappeared.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and the others did not know. They returned and examined the old storehouses, where they found the instrument. Its form matched Fang's writings, but they still could not determine the slackness or tightness of its strings. The sounds could not be written down for people of the time; those who knew them wished to teach but had no starting point, and those whose minds grasped them understood physically but had no teacher. Thus the scribal officials able to distinguish clear and turbid tones disappeared.

sentences.zh: 其可以相傳者，唯大搉常數及候氣而已。

translations.literal: What could be transmitted were only the rough constant numbers and the methods for observing qi.
translations.idiomatic: What could be transmitted were only the rough constant numbers and the methods for observing qi.

sentences.zh: 夫五音生於陰陽，分為十二律，轉生六十，皆所以紀鬥氣，效物類也。

translations.literal: The five notes arise from yin and yang, divide into the twelve pitch-pipes, and turn to generate sixty; all serve to record the Dipper's qi and model the categories of things.
translations.idiomatic: The five notes arise from yin and yang, divide into the twelve pitch-pipes, and turn to generate sixty; all serve to record the Dipper's qi and model the categories of things.

sentences.zh: 天效以景，地效以響，即律也。

translations.literal: Heaven gives its model through shadows, and earth gives its model through resonance; these are the pitch-pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gives its model through shadows, and earth gives its model through resonance; these are the pitch-pipes.

sentences.zh: 陰陽和則景至，律氣應則灰除。

translations.literal: When yin and yang are harmonious, the shadow arrives; when the qi of the pitch-pipes responds, the ashes are expelled.
translations.idiomatic: When yin and yang are harmonious, the shadow arrives; when the qi of the pitch-pipes responds, the ashes are expelled.

sentences.zh: 是故天子常以日冬夏至御前殿，合八能之士，陳八音，聽樂均，度晷景，候鐘律，權土灰，放陰陽。

translations.literal: Therefore, on the days of the winter and summer solstices, the Son of Heaven would regularly go to the front hall, gather the men of the eight abilities, array the eight sounds, listen to the tuning of the music, measure the gnomon shadow, observe the bells and pitch-pipes, weigh the earth and ashes, and imitate yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, on the days of the winter and summer solstices, the Son of Heaven would regularly go to the front hall, gather the men of the eight abilities, array the eight sounds, listen to the tuning of the music, measure the gnomon shadow, observe the bells and pitch-pipes, weigh the earth and ashes, and imitate yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 冬至陽氣應，則樂均清，景長極，黃鐘通，土灰輕而衡仰。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice, when yang qi responds, the musical tuning is clear, the shadow reaches its maximum length, Huangzhong is open, and the earth and ashes are light, so the balance rises.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice, when yang qi responds, the musical tuning is clear, the shadow reaches its maximum length, Huangzhong is open, and the earth and ashes are light, so the balance rises.

sentences.zh: 夏至陰氣應，則樂均濁，景短極，蕤賓通，土灰重而衡低[15]。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice, when yin qi responds, the musical tuning is turbid, the shadow reaches its maximum shortness, Ruibin is open, and the earth and ashes are heavy, so the balance sinks [15].
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice, when yin qi responds, the musical tuning is turbid, the shadow reaches its maximum shortness, Ruibin is open, and the earth and ashes are heavy, so the balance sinks [15].

sentences.zh: 進退於先後五日之中，八能各以候狀聞，太史封上。

translations.literal: Within five days before or after the appointed time, each of the men of the eight abilities reported the observed conditions, and the Grand Scribe sealed and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Within five days before or after the appointed time, each of the men of the eight abilities reported the observed conditions, and the Grand Scribe sealed and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 效則和，否則占[16]。

translations.literal: If the signs matched, there was harmony; if not, divination was made [16].
translations.idiomatic: If the signs matched, there was harmony; if not, divination was made [16].

sentences.zh: 候氣之法，為室三重，戶閉，塗釁必周，密佈緹縵。

translations.literal: For the method of observing qi, a chamber of three layers was made, the doors were closed, the plastering and sealing were made complete, and red silk curtains were densely arranged.
translations.idiomatic: For the method of observing qi, a chamber of three layers was made, the doors were closed, the plastering and sealing were made complete, and red silk curtains were densely arranged.

sentences.zh: 室中以木為案，每律各一，內庳外高，從其方位，加律其上，以葭莩灰抑其內端[17]，案歷而候之。

translations.literal: Inside the chamber, wooden stands were set up, one for each pitch-pipe. The inner side was low and the outer side high, following their directions. The pitch-pipes were placed on them, reed-membrane ashes were pressed against their inner ends [17], and they were observed according to the calendar.

The pitch-pipes were placed on them, reed-membrane ashes were pressed against their inner ends [17], and they were observed according to the calendar.

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances, Chapters and Sentences says: "Darao investigated the nature of the five phases and observed what the Dipper handle established. Thereupon he first made jia and yi to name the days, calling them stems, and made zi and chou to name the months, calling them branches. Branches and stems are paired to complete the cycle of sixty."

translations.idiomatic: Taking one third from gong generates zhi. The number of zhi is fifty-four; Linzhong is six cun long, and six times nine is fifty-four.

translations.idiomatic: Adding one third to zhi generates shang. The number of shang is seventy-two; Taicu is eight cun long, and eight times nine is seventy-two.

translations.idiomatic: Taking one third from shang generates yu. The number of yu is forty-eight; Nanlu is five cun and one third of a cun long, and five times nine is forty-five plus one third of a cun, making forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 三分羽益一生角，角數六十四，姑洗長七寸九分寸之一，七九六十三又九分寸之一，為六十四也。

translations.literal: Adding one third to yu generates jue. The number of jue is sixty-four; Guxian is seven cun and one ninth of a cun long, and seven times nine is sixty-three plus one ninth of a cun, making sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 自此已後，則隨月而變，所謂『還相為宮。』」

translations.literal: Thus the transforming action of yin and yang and the end and beginning of the myriad things are both arrayed among the pitch-pipes and standards and pass through the days and branches, so the nature of change can be seen."

sentences.zh: 前書注曰：「章帝時，零陵文學奚景於泠道縣舜祠下得白玉琯管。

translations.literal: The commentary to the Former Han says: "In the time of Emperor Zhang, Xi Jing, a scholar of Lingling, obtained a white jade pitch-pipe beneath the shrine to Shun in Lingdao County.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary to the Former Han says: "In the time of Emperor Zhang, Xi Jing, a scholar of Lingling, obtained a white jade pitch-pipe beneath the shrine to Shun in Lingdao County.

sentences.zh: 古以玉為琯。」

translations.literal: In antiquity, jade was used to make pitch-pipes."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, jade was used to make pitch-pipes."

sentences.zh: 薛瑩書曰，上以太常樂丞鮑鄴等上樂事，下車騎將軍馬防。

translations.literal: Xue Ying's letter says that, because Music Assistant Bao Ye and others of the Grand Music Office had submitted matters concerning music, the emperor sent the matter down to General of Chariots and Cavalry Ma Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying's letter says that, because Music Assistant Bao Ye and others of the Grand Music Office had submitted matters concerning music, the emperor sent the matter down to General of Chariots and Cavalry Ma Fang.

sentences.zh: 防奏言：「建初二年七月，鄴上言：『王者飲食，必道須四時五味，故有食舉之樂，所以順天地，養神明，求福應也。

translations.literal: Fang memorialized: "In the seventh month of Jianchu 2, Ye submitted: 'In the ruler's food and drink, the proper way must require the four seasons and five flavors. Therefore there is music for raising food, by which Heaven and Earth are followed, spirits are nourished, and auspicious responses are sought.
translations.idiomatic: Fang memorialized: "In the seventh month of Jianchu 2, Ye submitted: 'In the ruler's food and drink, the proper way must require the four seasons and five flavors. Therefore there is music for raising food, by which Heaven and Earth are followed, spirits are nourished, and auspicious responses are sought.

sentences.zh: 移風易俗，莫善於樂。

translations.literal: For transforming customs and changing practices, nothing is better than music.
translations.idiomatic: For transforming customs and changing practices, nothing is better than music.

sentences.zh: 樂者天地之和，不可久廢。

translations.literal: Music is the harmony of Heaven and Earth and cannot long be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Music is the harmony of Heaven and Earth and cannot long be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 今官樂但有太蔟，皆不應月律。

translations.literal: Now official music has only Taicu, and none of it corresponds to the monthly pitch-pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Now official music has only Taicu, and none of it corresponds to the monthly pitch-pipes.

sentences.zh: 可作十二月均，各應其月氣，乃能順天地，和氣宜應。

translations.literal: The tunings for the twelve months should be made, each corresponding to the qi of its month; only then can they accord with Heaven and Earth and make harmony and qi respond properly.
translations.idiomatic: The tunings for the twelve months should be made, each corresponding to the qi of its month; only then can they accord with Heaven and Earth and make harmony and qi respond properly.

sentences.zh: 明帝始令靈台六律候，而未設其門。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming first ordered observations of the six pitch-pipes at the Numinous Terrace, but had not yet established their gates.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming first ordered observations of the six pitch-pipes at the Numinous Terrace, but had not yet established their gates.

sentences.zh: 樂經曰十二月行之，所以宣氣豐物也。

translations.literal: The Classic of Music says that it is performed through the twelve months in order to spread qi and enrich things.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Music says that it is performed through the twelve months in order to spread qi and enrich things.

sentences.zh: 月開斗建之門，而奏歌其律。

translations.literal: Each month opens the gate established by the Dipper and performs songs in its pitch-pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Each month opens the gate established by the Dipper and performs songs in its pitch-pipe.

sentences.zh: 誠宜施行。

translations.literal: It truly ought to be put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: It truly ought to be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 願與待詔嚴崇及能作樂器者共作治，考工給所當。』

translations.literal: I request that, together with Expectant Appointee Yan Chong and those able to make musical instruments, we jointly make and repair them, with the Office of Works supplying what is needed.'
translations.idiomatic: I request that, together with Expectant Appointee Yan Chong and those able to make musical instruments, we jointly make and repair them, with the Office of Works supplying what is needed.'

sentences.zh: 詔下太常。

translations.literal: The edict sent this down to the Grand Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: The edict sent this down to the Grand Music Office.

sentences.zh: 太常上言：『作樂器直錢百四十六萬，請太僕作成上。』

translations.literal: The Grand Music Office submitted: 'Making the musical instruments will cost 1,460,000 cash. We request that the Grand Coachman have them completed and submitted.'
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Music Office submitted: 'Making the musical instruments will cost 1,460,000 cash. We request that the Grand Coachman have them completed and submitted.'

sentences.zh: 奏寢。

translations.literal: The memorial was set aside.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was set aside.

sentences.zh: 今明詔下臣防，臣輒問鄴及待詔知音律者，皆言聖人作樂，所以宣氣致和，順陰陽也。

translations.literal: Now that Your enlightened edict has been sent down to me, Fang, I have accordingly asked Ye and the Expectant Appointees who know music and pitch-pipes. They all say that sages made music in order to spread qi, bring harmony, and accord with yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your enlightened edict has been sent down to me, Fang, I have accordingly asked Ye and the Expectant Appointees who know music and pitch-pipes. They all say that sages made music in order to spread qi, bring harmony, and accord with yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為可順上天之明待，因歲首令正，發太蔟之律，奏雅頌之音，以立太平，以迎和氣。

translations.literal: In my foolish opinion, we may accord with the bright timing of High Heaven by issuing correct commands at the beginning of the year, sounding the pitch-pipe of Taicu, and performing the sounds of the Odes and Hymns, in order to establish great peace and welcome harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: In my foolish opinion, we may accord with the bright timing of High Heaven by issuing correct commands at the beginning of the year, sounding the pitch-pipe of Taicu, and performing the sounds of the Odes and Hymns, in order to establish great peace and welcome harmonious qi.

translations.literal: Its regulations are very complete."
translations.idiomatic: Its regulations are very complete."

sentences.zh: 詔書以防言下三公。

translations.literal: The edict took Fang's words and sent them down to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: The edict took Fang's words and sent them down to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 淮南子曰：「水勝故夏至濕，火勝故冬至燥。

translations.literal: The Huainanzi says, "Because water prevails, the summer solstice is damp; because fire prevails, the winter solstice is dry.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says, "Because water prevails, the summer solstice is damp; because fire prevails, the winter solstice is dry.

sentences.zh: 燥故灰輕，濕故灰重。」

translations.literal: Because it is dry, the ashes are light; because it is damp, the ashes are heavy."
translations.idiomatic: Because it is dry, the ashes are light; because it is damp, the ashes are heavy."

sentences.zh: 易緯曰：「冬至人主不出宮，寢兵，從樂五日，擊黃鐘之磬。

translations.literal: The Apocrypha of the Changes says, "At the winter solstice the ruler does not leave the palace, rests the troops, follows the music for five days, and strikes the chime-stone of Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Apocrypha of the Changes says, "At the winter solstice the ruler does not leave the palace, rests the troops, follows the music for five days, and strikes the chime-stone of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 公卿大夫列士之意得，則陰陽之晷如度數。

translations.literal: When the intentions of dukes, ministers, grandees, and ranked officers are fulfilled, the yin-yang shadow accords with the degrees and numbers.
translations.idiomatic: When the intentions of dukes, ministers, grandees, and ranked officers are fulfilled, the yin-yang shadow accords with the degrees and numbers.

sentences.zh: 夏至之日，如冬至之禮。

translations.literal: On the day of the summer solstice, the same rites were performed as at the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the summer solstice, the same rites were performed as at the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 冬至之日，樹八尺之表，日中視其晷。

translations.literal: On the day of the winter solstice, an eight-chi gnomon was set up, and at midday its shadow was observed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the winter solstice, an eight-chi gnomon was set up, and at midday its shadow was observed.

sentences.zh: 晷如度者其歲美，人民和順。

translations.literal: When the shadow accords with the degrees, the year is good and the people are harmonious and compliant.
translations.idiomatic: When the shadow accords with the degrees, the year is good and the people are harmonious and compliant.

sentences.zh: 晷不如度者則歲惡，人民多斗言，政令為之不平。

translations.literal: When the shadow does not accord with the degrees, the year is bad, the people have many disputes, and government orders become uneven.
translations.idiomatic: When the shadow does not accord with the degrees, the year is bad, the people have many disputes, and government orders become uneven.

sentences.zh: 晷進則水，晷退則旱。

translations.literal: If the shadow advances, there is flood; if the shadow retreats, there is drought.
translations.idiomatic: If the shadow advances, there is flood; if the shadow retreats, there is drought.

sentences.zh: 進一尺則日食，退一尺則月食。

translations.literal: If it advances by one chi, there is a solar eclipse; if it retreats by one chi, there is a lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If it advances by one chi, there is a solar eclipse; if it retreats by one chi, there is a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 月食則正臣下之行，日食則正人主之道。」

translations.literal: When there is a lunar eclipse, the conduct of ministers and subordinates is corrected; when there is a solar eclipse, the way of the ruler is corrected."
translations.idiomatic: When there is a lunar eclipse, the conduct of ministers and subordinates is corrected; when there is a solar eclipse, the way of the ruler is corrected."

sentences.zh: 葭莩出河內。

translations.literal: Reed membrane comes from Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Reed membrane comes from Henei.

sentences.zh: 月令章句曰：「古之為鐘律者，以耳齊其聲。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances, Chapters and Sentences says, "In antiquity, those who made bells and pitch-pipes used the ear to align their sounds.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances, Chapters and Sentences says, "In antiquity, those who made bells and pitch-pipes used the ear to align their sounds.

sentences.zh: 後不能，則假數以正其度，度數正則音亦正矣。

translations.literal: Later, when this could no longer be done, they borrowed numbers to correct their measures; when the measures and numbers were correct, the sounds were also correct.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when this could no longer be done, they borrowed numbers to correct their measures; when the measures and numbers were correct, the sounds were also correct.

sentences.zh: 鐘以斤兩尺寸中所容受升斗之數為法，律亦以寸分長短為度。

translations.literal: For bells, the method was based on their jin and liang, their chi and cun, and the number of sheng and dou they could contain; pitch-pipes likewise used cun and fen, length and shortness, as their measure.
translations.idiomatic: For bells, the method was based on their jin and liang, their chi and cun, and the number of sheng and dou they could contain; pitch-pipes likewise used cun and fen, length and shortness, as their measure.

sentences.zh: 故曰黃鐘之管長九寸，徑三分，圍九分，其餘皆補短，雖大小圍數無增減。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said that the tube of Huangzhong is nine cun long, three fen in diameter, and nine fen in circumference; all the rest are made up from the shorter ones, and although they differ in size, their circumferential numbers do not increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said that the tube of Huangzhong is nine cun long, three fen in diameter, and nine fen in circumference; all the rest are made up from the shorter ones, and although they differ in size, their circumferential numbers do not increase or decrease.
